description: The bar chart illustrates the percentage point difference in morphosyntactic probing performance between two multilingual BERT models — mBERT (light blue) and XLM-R (dark blue) — across four different classifier configurations, as reported in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The horizontal axis lists the classifier architectures: “hidden:[50], linear,” “hidden:[], linear,” “hidden:[100], ReLU,” and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” indicating the hidden layer sizes and activation functions used in the probing classifiers. The vertical axis, labeled “% point difference,” ranges from –0.2 to +0.2, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1, representing the performance gap (XLM-R minus mBERT) on a per-language or aggregate probing task. For “hidden:[50], linear,” mBERT outperforms XLM-R by approximately 0.15 percentage points (negative bar), while XLM-R slightly underperforms (–0.05). In “hidden:[], linear,” both models show positive gains for XLM-R, with mBERT at ~+0.09 and XLM-R at ~+0.20. For “hidden:[100], ReLU,” mBERT underperforms by ~–0.12, while XLM-R shows a small positive gain (~+0.03). Finally, in “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” mBERT underperforms by ~–0.18 and XLM-R by ~–0.15. The chart visually emphasizes that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT in linear classifiers without hidden layers, while mBERT tends to perform better in more complex ReLU-based architectures, though both models show negative differences in those cases. Bars are grouped by classifier type, with mBERT always shown first (left) in each pair, and no sorting by magnitude is applied.
